contract: The file-bearing routes real clients fetch (public share track/cover, feed cover/enclosure, item cover/ebook/file download, item download) serve the exact file bytes with the route's client MIME (audio/mp4 for m4b, audio/mpeg for mp3, application/epub+zip, image/jpeg, image/jpg, application/zip); the sendFile layer advertises Accept-Ranges: bytes, serves a single closed/open/suffix range as 206 with exact Content-Range and Content-Length, ignores a multi-range header (200 full file) and answers malformed or unsatisfiable ranges 416 with Content-Range: bytes */size; every file response carries an ETag and Last-Modified, a matching If-None-Match or If-Modified-Since returns 304 with no body, a changed file revalidates with 200 and new bytes; HEAD mirrors GET headers without a body; download routes add Content-Disposition attachment with the item filename; a revoked share or a removed file answers 404 with no file bytes. The ETag algorithm itself is not contract.
exceptions: force is not applicable: byte ranges and conditional reads have no force/refresh mode; a client revalidates with If-None-Match/If-Modified-Since or changes the URL.
The ETag format is deliberately not asserted; only round-trip behaviour is contract.

invariants.contract: The share track, feed enclosure, ebook, feed cover and raw item cover each return 200 with the exact fixture file bytes and the MIME the route sets (audio/mp4, audio/mp4, application/epub+zip, image/jpg, image/jpeg); the sendFile-backed routes advertise Accept-Ranges: bytes and a Content-Length equal to the file size, while the streamed feed cover does neither.

A single closed range on a sendFile route answers 206 with Content-Range bytes a-b/size, Content-Length b-a+1 and exactly the file's a..b bytes; an open range a- answers a..end; a suffix range -N answers the last N bytes; an end past the file is clamped to the last byte; a multi-range header is not honoured and answers the complete file as 200 (no multipart/byteranges); a malformed range and a range starting at or past the size each answer 416 with Content-Range bytes */size and a short error body without file bytes.

A sendFile 200 carries an ETag and Last-Modified; If-None-Match with that ETag and If-Modified-Since with that value each answer 304 with no body and the same ETag; a different ETag answers 200 with the unchanged bytes; after the file on disk changes the old ETag answers 200 with the new length/bytes and a new ETag, whose If-None-Match answers 304; a streamed response without an ETag (feed cover) answers 200 to any If-None-Match.

HEAD of the feed enclosure, the ebook and a file download returns the GET status, Content-Type, Content-Length, Accept-Ranges, ETag, Last-Modified and Content-Disposition with an empty body; HEAD of an unknown feed cover returns 404 with no body.

GET /api/items/:id/file/:fileid/download of an ebook answers 200 with Content-Type application/epub+zip, Content-Disposition attachment; filename="Ebook Only.epub" and the exact ebook bytes; the inline /file/:fileid route serves the same bytes without Content-Disposition; an m4b file download is audio/mp4 for curl but audio/m4b for an Apple mobile WebKit user agent; GET /api/items/:id/download of a folder item and the public share download answer 200 with an application/zip attachment named after the item title and a ZIP body, not the raw audio bytes.

After an admin deletes a media-item share, its slug's track and cover routes answer 404 for the old share cookie and return no media bytes; after the item cover file is removed from disk, the raw cover route answers 404 with no image bytes.
